# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Howden_2025_antisecretory_mbma"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Howden_2025_antisecretory_mbma"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13235>

Howden et al. (2025) pooled two literature datasets: healthy-volunteer 24 h
intragastric pH-metry studies, summarised per drug and dose as the mean
percentage of a day with intragastric pH > 4 (the pH > 4 holding-time ratio,
HTR), and randomized erosive esophagitis healing trials, summarised per drug,
dose and week as the pooled healing rate. Merged by regimen, the two datasets
give one HTR and one healing rate (with its standard error) per arm and week.
The final model is a sigmoid Emax function of HTR on the **logit** of the
healing rate, with a separate HTR50 for week 4 and week 8, and two nested
random effects (between drug and between treatment within drug) that are both
scaled by the arm's standard error.

The model simulates arm-level healing rates, not patients: each simulated
`id` is one hypothetical study arm.

# Population

* 82 phase I pH-metry studies in healthy volunteers (4297 participants in 201
  dose arms; pH recorded between days 5 and 8 of daily dosing).
* 104 phase II/III randomized erosive esophagitis healing trials (43,417
  patients in 196 treatment arms, intention-to-treat healing rates at week 4
  and/or week 8). The abstract gives 103 trials; the Results and Figure 1 give
  104.
* Regimens: placebo; the H2-receptor antagonists (H2RA) famotidine,
  nizatidine and ranitidine; the proton pump inhibitors (PPI) esomeprazole,
  lansoprazole, omeprazole, pantoprazole, rabeprazole, azeloprazole,
  dexlansoprazole and ilaprazole; and the potassium-competitive acid blockers
  (P-CAB) tegoprazan and vonoprazan (Table 1).
* Adults (search restricted to participants >= 18 years); MEDLINE and Embase
  up to 31 March 2023.

The same information is available programmatically via
`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Howden_2025_antisecretory_mbma"))$population`.

# Source trace

The model is given in full as a NONMEM `$PRED` block ("Final Model Code") in
the paper's supplement; the parameter values are the final estimates of
Supplementary Table S2. With `HR` the healing rate of arm `i` of drug `d`:

$$
\mathrm{logit}(HR_{di}) = \mathrm{logit}(E_0) + \frac{HTR^{\gamma}\,[\mathrm{logit}(E_{\max}) - \mathrm{logit}(E_0)]}{E_{HTR,50}^{\gamma} + HTR^{\gamma}}
+ SE_{di}\,\omega_{BDV}\,\eta_d + SE_{di}\,\omega_{BTV}\,\varepsilon_{di},
\qquad \eta_d, \varepsilon_{di} \sim N(0, 1)
$$

with $\omega_{BDV} = \mathrm{logit}((BDV + 50)/100)$ and likewise for BTV.

| Quantity | Model name | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Placebo (HTR = 0) healing rate E0 | `logite0` | logit(12.3%) | Table S2 (RSE 68.9%) |
| Maximum healing rate Emax | `logitemax` | logit(95.9%) | Table S2 (RSE 2.3%) |
| HTR50, week 8 | `lec50_wk8` | log(26.9%) | Table S2 (RSE 21.6%) |
| HTR50, week 4 | `lec50_wk4` | log(45.7%) | Table S2 (RSE 22.0%); code `IF(WEEK.EQ.1) TVEPH50 = THETA(7)` |
| HTR50 non-approval effect | `e_trt_approved_ec50` | -46.5% (applied when `TRT_APPROVED = 0`) | Table S2 (RSE 4.5%); code `IF(APPR.EQ.0)` |
| HTR50 P-CAB effect | `e_trt_pcab_ec50` | -30.8% | Table S2 (RSE 45.1%); code `CLASS.EQ.5` |
| HTR50 H2RA effect | `e_trt_h2ra_ec50` | +41.3% | Table S2 (RSE 21.8%); code `CLASS.EQ.3` |
| Shape gamma | `lhill` | log(1.31) | Table S2 (RSE 33.5%) |
| Between-drug variability | `bdv_pct` | 8.1 (% above 50% at SE = 1) | Table S2 (RSE 27.8%) |
| Between-treatment variability | `btv_pct` | 6.86 (% above 50% at SE = 1) | Table S2 (RSE 25.8%) |
| BTV approval effect | `e_trt_approved_btv` | +205% (applied when `TRT_APPROVED = 1`) | Table S2 (RSE 48.7%); code `IF(APPR.EQ.1)`, see Assumptions |
| BTV H2RA effect | `e_trt_h2ra_btv` | -71% | Table S2 (RSE 13.0%); code `CLASS.EQ.3` |
| Drug random effect | `eta_drug_mu` | variance 1, fixed | `$OMEGA (1 FIX)`, `BDV_ = TVBDV_*ETA(1)` |
| Treatment random effect | `addSd` | SD 1, fixed | `$SIGMA (1 FIX)`, `BTV_ = TVBTV_*EPS(1)` |
| Arm SE scaling of both random effects | `SE_ARM` | per record | code `IPRED = MU + EEHR_SE*BDV_ + EEHR_SE*BTV_` |
| Logit link and Emax structure | `mu`, `logit_ee_healing` | -- | code `MU = EEHR0_ + PH4**GAMMA*(...)`; Figure 2 |

# Analysis dataset (Table 1)

The arms below carry Table 1's pooled HTR and observed healing rates. The
approval flags follow the Table 1 footnote (nizatidine, ranitidine 300 mg
once daily, azeloprazole and ilaprazole not approved; pantoprazole 80 mg once
daily also flagged). Tegoprazan, which is not approved in the US or the EU,
is coded as not approved.

arms <- tab1 |>
  pivot_longer(c(hr_wk4, hr_wk8), names_to = "wk", values_to = "hr_obs") |>
  filter(!is.na(hr_obs)) |>
  mutate(week = ifelse(wk == "hr_wk4", 4, 8)) |>

class_cov <- function(cls) {
  data.frame(
    TRT_H2RA = as.integer(cls == "H2RA"),

# Typical response and prediction interval (Figure 4)

Figure 4 of the paper is a visual predictive check of approved regimens: the
typical healing-rate curve per drug class and week, with an 80% prediction
interval for large studies (SE = 0.25, about 300 patients). The curves below
are the model's typical values (`zeroRe()`); the shaded bands are the 10th
and 90th percentiles of 200 simulated arms per HTR grid point. The dots are
Table 1's observed approved-regimen healing rates.

```{r fig4-sim}
# eta_drug_mu shifts the model() quantity mu rather than an ini() parameter,
# so rxode2 warns that it is not mu-referenced; the typical-value copy has no
# omega or sigma left, which rxode2 also reports on every solve. Both are
# expected here and are silenced so the article shows only real problems.
mod <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Howden_2025_antisecretory_mbma")))
mod_typ <- suppressWarnings(zeroRe(mod))
classes <- c("H2RA", "PPI", "P-CAB")
grid <- expand.grid(
  GASTRIC_PH4_TIME_PCT = seq(0, 100, by = 4),
  class = classes,
  week = c(4, 8),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
grid <- cbind(grid, class_cov(grid$class))
grid$TRT_APPROVED <- 1
grid$SE_ARM <- 0.25
grid$point <- seq_len(nrow(grid))

typ_ev <- grid |>
  mutate(id = point, time = week, evid = 0, amt = 0)
typ <- as.data.frame(suppressWarnings(rxSolve(mod_typ, typ_ev, keep = c("class", "week"))))

n_rep <- 200
sim_ev <- grid[rep(seq_len(nrow(grid)), each = n_rep), ] |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()), time = week, evid = 0, amt = 0)
rxSetSeed(20250101)
sim <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, sim_ev,
  keep = c("class", "week", "point"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
))
sim$hr_sim <- 100 * plogis(sim$sim)

band <- sim |>
  group_by(class, week, GASTRIC_PH4_TIME_PCT) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(hr_sim, 0.1), hi = quantile(hr_sim, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Howden 2025: typical healing rate (line) and 80% prediction interval for SE = 0.25 studies (band) of approved regimens, with Table 1 approved-regimen observations (dots)."}
obs_appr <- arms |>
  filter(approved == 1, class %in% classes)
ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = band,
    aes(GASTRIC_PH4_TIME_PCT, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = class), alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_line(data = typ, aes(GASTRIC_PH4_TIME_PCT, ee_healing, colour = class)) +
  geom_point(data = obs_appr, aes(htr, hr_obs, colour = class)) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("Week", week)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Mean time with intragastric pH > 4 (% of 24 h)",
    y = "Erosive esophagitis healing rate (%)",
    colour = "Drug class", fill = "Drug class"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

At HTR = 0 every curve starts at the placebo healing rate E0 = 12.3%, and at
100% HTR the week-8 PPI and P-CAB curves reach about 92-93%, as in Figure 4.

```{r fig4-check}
e0 <- typ |>
  filter(GASTRIC_PH4_TIME_PCT == 0, class == "PPI", week == 8)
w8_top <- typ |>
  filter(GASTRIC_PH4_TIME_PCT == 100, week == 8) |>
  select(class, ee_healing)
w8_top
stopifnot(
  abs(e0$ee_healing - 12.3) < 1,
  all(w8_top$ee_healing[w8_top$class != "H2RA"] > 90),
  all(w8_top$ee_healing[w8_top$class != "H2RA"] < 95.9)
)
```

# Required pH > 4 holding time (Table S3)

Table S3 lists the hours per day of pH > 4 that the **typical** approved
regimen of each class needs to reach a healing rate of 80%, 85% or 90%.
Inverting the Emax model for HTR gives

$$
HTR_{req} = E_{HTR,50}\left(\frac{f}{1 - f}\right)^{1/\gamma},\qquad
f = \frac{\mathrm{logit}(p) - \mathrm{logit}(E_0)}{\mathrm{logit}(E_{\max}) - \mathrm{logit}(E_0)},
$$

"not achievable" when the result exceeds 100%. The closed form is checked
against the model by solving it at the required HTR, which must return the
target healing rate.

```{r tableS3-hours}
th <- as.list(rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta)
ec50_class <- function(cls, week) {
  base <- exp(if (week == 4) th$lec50_wk4 else th$lec50_wk8)
  base * (1 + th$e_trt_pcab_ec50 * (cls == "P-CAB")) *
    (1 + th$e_trt_h2ra_ec50 * (cls == "H2RA"))
}
req <- expand.grid(
  target = c(80, 85, 90), class = classes, week = c(4, 8),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
req$f <- (qlogis(req$target / 100) - th$logite0) / (th$logitemax - th$logite0)
req$htr_req <- mapply(ec50_class, req$class, req$week) *
  (req$f / (1 - req$f))^(1 / exp(th$lhill))
req$hours <- ifelse(req$htr_req > 100, NA, req$htr_req / 100 * 24)

# Self-consistency: the model solved at the required HTR returns the target.
chk_ev <- req |>
  filter(!is.na(hours)) |>
  mutate(
    id = seq_len(n()), time = week, evid = 0, amt = 0,
    GASTRIC_PH4_TIME_PCT = htr_req, TRT_APPROVED = 1, SE_ARM = 0.5
  )
chk_ev <- cbind(chk_ev, class_cov(chk_ev$class))
chk <- as.data.frame(suppressWarnings(rxSolve(mod_typ, chk_ev, keep = "target")))
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$ee_healing - chk$target)) < 1e-6)

paper_hours <- tibble::tribble(
  ~target, ~class, ~week, ~paper,
  80, "H2RA", 4, NA, 80, "H2RA", 8, 15.3,
  80, "PPI", 4, 17.7, 80, "PPI", 8, 10.5,
  80, "P-CAB", 4, 12.0, 80, "P-CAB", 8, 7.2,
  85, "H2RA", 4, NA, 85, "H2RA", 8, 19.5,
  85, "PPI", 4, 22.6, 85, "PPI", 8, 13.5,
  85, "P-CAB", 4, 15.4, 85, "P-CAB", 8, 9.2,
  90, "H2RA", 4, NA, 90, "H2RA", 8, NA,
  90, "PPI", 4, NA, 90, "PPI", 8, 20.5,
  90, "P-CAB", 4, 23.4, 90, "P-CAB", 8, 14.0
)
hours_cmp <- req |>
  select(target, class, week, hours) |>
  left_join(paper_hours, by = c("target", "class", "week")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (hours - paper) / paper) |>
  arrange(target, class, week)
hours_cmp |>
  mutate(hours = round(hours, 1), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    "Target healing rate (%)" = target, "Drug class" = class, "Week" = week,
    "Required h/day (model)" = hours, "Required h/day (Table S3)" = paper,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Every entry the paper marks "not achievable" is also above 100% HTR here,
and the achievable entries agree within a few percent (rounding of the
Table S2 estimates, notably gamma = 1.31, moves the inverted HTR by that
much).

```{r tableS3-hours-check}
stopifnot(
  identical(is.na(hours_cmp$hours), is.na(hours_cmp$paper)),
  max(abs(hours_cmp$pct_diff), na.rm = TRUE) < 5
)
```

# Probability of achieving a target healing rate (Table S3, Figure 6)

The paper simulated each drug class at its aggregated HTR levels for studies
with SE = 0.5 (about 100 patients) and reported the fraction of simulated
studies reaching a healing rate of at least 80%, 85% or 90%. Only approved
regimens enter the simulations. Because both random effects are normal on the
logit scale, the probability for one arm is exact:
`1 - pnorm((logit(p) - mu) / (SE_ARM * sqrt(sdDrug^2 + sdTrt^2)))`, using the
model's own `mu`, `sdDrug` and `sdTrt`. The class probability averages this
over the class's approved arms observed at that week. The Table S3 "average
time observed" (7.5 h H2RA, 13.7 h PPI, 20.0 h P-CAB) guides the arm sets:
the PPI value is the mean of the approved PPI regimens of Table 1, and the
P-CAB value is the mean of the three vonoprazan regimens, which excludes
tegoprazan. No H2RA subset gives 7.5 h exactly (the two approved regimens
give 8.7 h, adding nizatidine 7.3 h, all four 7.6 h); the H2RA probabilities
are zero for every choice.

```{r tableS3-prob}
sim_arms <- arms |>
  filter(class %in% classes, approved == 1)
sim_arms |>
  distinct(class, drug, regimen, htr) |>
  group_by(class) |>
  summarise(mean_hours = round(mean(htr) / 100 * 24, 1)) |>
  rename("Drug class" = class, "Mean pH > 4 time (h/day)" = mean_hours) |>
  knitr::kable()

prob_ev <- sim_arms |>
  mutate(
    id = seq_len(n()), time = week, evid = 0, amt = 0,
    GASTRIC_PH4_TIME_PCT = htr, TRT_APPROVED = 1, SE_ARM = 0.5
  )
prob_ev <- cbind(prob_ev, class_cov(prob_ev$class))
prob_typ <- as.data.frame(suppressWarnings(rxSolve(mod_typ, prob_ev,
  keep = "class"
)))

prob_model <- prob_typ |>
  crossing(target = c(80, 85, 90)) |>
  mutate(
    p_arm = 1 - pnorm((qlogis(target / 100) - mu) /
      (SE_ARM * sqrt(sdDrug^2 + sdTrt^2)))
  ) |>
  group_by(target, class, week = time) |>
  summarise(model = 100 * mean(p_arm), .groups = "drop")

# Stochastic cross-check: 200 simulated studies per arm.
n_rep <- 200
mc_ev <- prob_ev[rep(seq_len(nrow(prob_ev)), each = n_rep), ] |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
rxSetSeed(20250102)
mc <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, mc_ev, keep = "class", returnType = "data.frame"))
mc$hr_sim <- 100 * plogis(mc$sim)
prob_mc <- mc |>
  crossing(target = c(80, 85, 90)) |>
  group_by(target, class, week = time) |>
  summarise(simulated = 100 * mean(hr_sim >= target), .groups = "drop")

paper_prob <- tibble::tribble(
  ~target, ~class, ~week, ~paper,
  80, "H2RA", 4, 0.0, 80, "H2RA", 8, 0.0,
  80, "PPI", 4, 19.7, 80, "PPI", 8, 75.5,
  80, "P-CAB", 4, 90.0, 80, "P-CAB", 8, 99.2,
  85, "H2RA", 4, 0.0, 85, "H2RA", 8, 0.0,
  85, "PPI", 4, 6.1, 85, "PPI", 8, 50.0,
  85, "P-CAB", 4, 70.9, 85, "P-CAB", 8, 95.4,
  90, "H2RA", 4, 0.0, 90, "H2RA", 8, 0.0,
  90, "PPI", 4, 0.6, 90, "PPI", 8, 17.3,
  90, "P-CAB", 4, 35.1, 90, "P-CAB", 8, 74.1
)
prob_cmp <- prob_model |>
  left_join(prob_mc, by = c("target", "class", "week")) |>
  left_join(paper_prob, by = c("target", "class", "week")) |>
  mutate(diff = model - paper) |>
  arrange(target, class, week)
prob_cmp |>
  mutate(across(c(model, simulated, diff), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename(
    "Target healing rate (%)" = target, "Drug class" = class, "Week" = week,
    "P(success) exact (%)" = model, "P(success) simulated (%)" = simulated,
    "P(success) Table S3 (%)" = paper, "Exact minus paper (points)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r fig6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 6 of Howden 2025: probability of a study (SE = 0.5) achieving at least the target healing rate, by drug class and week. Bars are the model; crosses are Table S3."}
ggplot(prob_cmp, aes(paste("Week", week), model, fill = class)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = paper),
    position = position_dodge(0.9), shape = 4, size = 2.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste0("Minimum healing rate ", target, "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Probability of achieving healing rate (%)", fill = "Drug class") +
  theme_bw()
```

The P-CAB probabilities reproduce Table S3 to within about one percentage
point and the H2RA probabilities are zero, as in the paper. The PPI
probabilities agree to within about three points; the paper does not list
which PPI regimens it counted as approved, and the Table 1 approval
footnotes, which are used here, reproduce its 13.7 h average but not every
probability exactly.

```{r tableS3-prob-check}
pc <- split(prob_cmp, prob_cmp$class)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(pc[["P-CAB"]]$diff)) < 1.5,
  max(pc[["H2RA"]]$model) < 0.5,
  max(abs(pc[["PPI"]]$diff)) < 4,
  # The Monte Carlo estimate agrees with the exact average (200 studies per
  # arm; the binomial SE of a pooled class probability is below 2 points).
  max(abs(prob_cmp$simulated - prob_cmp$model)) < 6
)
```

# NCA

No NCA is performed: the model has no drug concentrations, doses or time
course. Its input is a regimen-level pharmacodynamic summary (HTR) and its
output is an arm-level healing rate at week 4 or week 8, so the validation
above uses the paper's own tabulated predictions instead of PKNCA.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Final estimates from Table S2, not the printed `$THETA` block.** The
  `$THETA` block of the supplement's Final Model Code lists a different set of
  numbers (e.g. E0 10.32, EHTR50 week 8 24.74, BTV approval effect 165.4).
  Those are initial or earlier-run values; Table S2 is used throughout. The
  check above (required hours and probabilities of success) reproduces
  Table S3 with the Table S2 values.
* **E0 = 12.3%.** The Results text gives the placebo healing rate as 10.6%
  (RSE 70%); Table S2 gives 12.3% (RSE 68.9%). The Table S2 value reproduces
  the Table S3 required holding times and the 12% intercept of Figure 4;
  10.6% does not.
* **Direction of the BTV approval effect.** Table S2 labels the +205% BTV
  effect "Non-approval effect", and its footnote says between-treatment
  variability was larger for non-approved treatments, but the Final Model
  Code applies it when `APPR.EQ.1` (approved). The code is followed: with it
  the simulated P-CAB week-8 probability of a >= 90% healing rate is 74%
  (Table S3: 74.1%), whereas applying the effect to non-approved regimens
  instead gives about 88%. In the model it therefore multiplies the
  between-treatment SD by 3.05 for approved regimens.
* **Week as observation time.** The NONMEM `WEEK` flag is encoded from the
  observation time: records at `time = 4` (weeks) use the week-4 HTR50 and
  records at `time = 8` the week-8 value. The model is only defined at those
  two times.
* **Between-drug random effect name.** `eta_drug_mu` acts on the logit-scale
  prediction `mu`, which is a `model()` quantity rather than an `ini()`
  parameter, so `checkModelConventions()` reports that it has no matching
  fixed effect. The name records the grouping level (drug) and the quantity
  it shifts, as in the source.
* **Arm sets for the Table S3 simulations.** The paper does not list the arms
  it simulated. Approved regimens per the Table 1 footnotes are used;
  tegoprazan is treated as not approved because it is not approved in the US
  or the EU, which is what the P-CAB 20.0 h average requires.
* **Placebo is not a drug class here.** Placebo arms have `TRT_H2RA = 0` and
  `TRT_PCAB = 0`, like PPI arms; the model distinguishes them only by their
  low HTR (10.2%).
